entropy_direction.power_note: Observed effect d=-1.36; this run could detect d>=0.50.
entropy_direction.note: high=bad means high entropy predicts failure -> bail early on high-entropy generations. high=good means high entropy predicts success -> verify high-entropy candidates first instead of bailing. none means entropy is not a usable signal for this model, which is a real and useful result, not a failed run. A direction is only reported when the difference survives a two-sided permutation test (p<0.05, 20000 resamples) AND exceeds a minimum separation of 0.08. raw_direction_before_gating is the unfiltered sign of the mean difference; it is recorded for transparency and must not be used as a finding.

signal_coverage.note: cv_* numbers are the honest estimate: the combination was rebuilt from scratch in each fold and scored on records that fold never saw. final_fit_stats describes the shipped combination measured on all the data it was fitted to, so it is optimistic by construction -- quote the cv numbers. A signal chosen in only one or two folds is a fitting artefact, not part of this model's pattern; signal_stability shows which held up.

null_test.note: The entire selection procedure was re-run on 40 label shuffles. Shuffled labels landing at ~0.5 means the procedure is not manufacturing structure. empirical_p has a floor of 1/41 = 0.024 -- it cannot report smaller than that no matter how strong the effect.

holdout_validation.verdict: held up on data it never saw
holdout_validation.note: The signal was chosen and its threshold fitted using the training records only; test_balanced_accuracy is measured on records that played no part in either decision, so it needs no correction for the number of candidates searched. A large drop from train to test means the search found noise. Both halves are small — treat the held-out number as a direction, not a precise estimate.

task_holdout_validation.verdict: generalized to tasks it never saw
task_holdout_validation.note: The split is by task: every generation of a held-out task was excluded from selection and fitting. This is the check for 'does the signal apply to new questions', which record-level holdout cannot answer. With few failing tasks this number is low-power — a pass is meaningful, a fail means 'not proven', not 'proven false'. If a signal was selected on the full run, transfer_estimate also shows how often THAT signal separates unseen tasks over 300 random task splits — it answers 'does the discovered signal travel', which selection-based validation cannot answer at this scale.

trust.note: Saves test execution, not generation tokens -- the generation is already paid for. Worth it when the test suite is expensive or when latency matters more than tokens. The defect count is the price.

two_sided.note: Ship the trust zone untested, regenerate the bail zone, test the band between them. Both cut points come from one fit on one signal, ordered so the zones cannot overlap. The band is what the signal cannot decide -- the honest residue, not a gap in the analysis.

trust.note: Saves test execution, not generation tokens -- the generation is already paid for. Worth it when the test suite is expensive or when latency matters more than tokens. The defect count is the price.

rule_recommendation.note: Every threshold was fitted inside cross-validation folds and scored on records that fold never saw. `cross_validated` is what the rule does on unseen output from this model. `rule` is the same procedure fitted to all the data, for use.

signal_scan.note: 183 candidate entropy statistics were tested against the same pass/fail data, so raw p-values are corrected for multiple comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg). A signal is only reported as usable if its corrected p clears alpha AND |d| >= 0.2. Signals listed in nominally_significant_but_not_surviving cleared p<0.05 on their own but not after correction — with this many tests, that is the expected behaviour of noise, not a lead. They are candidates for a pre-registered test on a fresh run, never findings.

spike_location.note: spike_quartile: 0=head(early), 3=tail(late). If fail spikes cluster in a different quartile than ok spikes, spike location is a useful incorrectness predictor for this model.

spike_threshold_calibrated.note: Fitted on think_frac, the signal that survived correction for 183 tested candidates -- not on max_entropy, which did not separate. balanced_accuracy compares to 0.5.

signal_failure_routing.note: Failures split into 2 clusters on n_tokens (separation score 1.93). Each cluster has a different best intervention. Based on 37 failures — treat as provisional when any cluster has fewer than 5 members.
